sources.quote: The third-party group Northwoods Future PAC has spent more than $2 million backing Alfonso’s campaign. It has received $1.5 million from the campaign account Duffy used when he represented the 7th Congressional District before Tiffany.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff; reports the full $1.5M from Duffy's old House account and $2M+ PAC spending for Alfonso

sources.quote: Duffy for Wisconsin has transferred $1.5 million to Northwoods Future PAC, a super PAC supporting Alfonso. That’s more than Alfonso’s entire campaign has raised alone and roughly half of the $3.125 million that Northwoods Future has raised
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff; names the committee, $1.5M, and that it is roughly half of the PAC's receipts; calls it his dormant congressional committee

sources.quote: Duffy for Wisconsin, a campaign committee originally created to help him win congressional elections, sent $1 million, or half of its holdings, to Northwoods Future PAC in 2025.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found; first $1M check, half the committee's holdings; reprinted by PBS Wisconsin, Wausau Pilot, Superior Telegram and others

sources.quote: A super political action committee backing Alfonso has received $1 million from Duffy's old congressional account and another $1 million from Republican megadonor Richard Uihlein, whose shipping and packaging business, Uline, is based in Wisconsin.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff national coverage; $1M figure only (before the second check was reported)

sources.quote: Northwoods Future PAC has reported roughly $2 million in independent expenditures in support of Alfonso.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff; PAC independent spending for Alfonso, for comparison with the lead's $2.2M-$3.2M

sources.quote: Federal records tell a different story, the Badger Project reported. Duffy's old campaign committee sent $1 million — half its holdings — to the Northwoods Future PAC, which spent all of it supporting Alfonso.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff; Duffy on air says the win is 'not because of me'; no source disputes the transfer itself

notes: Widely covered, starting with The Badger Project on 2026-03-24 ($1M check). The $1.5M total appears post-cutoff in WPR (2026-08-07) and Wigderson (2026-09-18, 'roughly half' of the PAC's $3.125M). No source found stating the lead's comparison that the $1M check is the biggest from any dormant campaign committee in 2025-26 (next: $215K), or that the committee raised $0 from donors. A search snippet attributed to WisPolitics ('$3.5 million in outside spending... $1.5 million in transfers') could not be verified: the WisPolitics page (2026-08-11) is behind a login wall, so it is not recorded. Axios (2026-06-10) returned 403. No disagreeing coverage found.
